name: Amistad National Recreation Area
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Amistad National Recreation Area was authorized by Congress in 1965 and established in 1990 along the U.S.–Mexico border near Del Rio, Texas. The recreation area surrounds Amistad Reservoir, a 64,860-acre international lake formed by the Amistad Dam on the Rio Grande, built jointly by the United States and Mexico. The region contains some of the oldest and best-preserved rock art in North America, with over 200 known pictograph sites created by hunter-gatherer peoples over a span of roughly 4,000 years. The Fate Bell Shelter and Panther Cave are among the most significant archaeological sites in the Lower Pecos Canyonlands.
